draft.title: How to Care for 925 Silver Jewellery: A Practical Guide
draft.metaTitle: 925 Silver Jewellery Care: Cleaning and Storage Guide
draft.metaDescription: Learn a gentle routine for silver jewellery, how to store pieces separately, and when a plated finish or delicate setting needs specialist care.

sections.heading: Start with the finish, not a cleaning shortcut
sections.text: A silver ring, an oxidised pendant and a gold-plated silver chain can need different care. Before choosing a cleaner, check the instructions for the individual piece. If the finish, stones or construction are uncertain, start by asking the maker rather than trying an aggressive home treatment. This guide is general care information; the directions supplied with your jewellery take priority.

sections.heading: Build a simple wearing routine
sections.text: Put jewellery on after applying fragrance, cosmetics and hair products. Remove it before swimming, household cleaning and activities that expose it to strong chemicals or impact. After wear, use a clean, soft cloth to remove surface residue gently. Check clasps and settings as you handle each piece; a loose part needs attention before the next wear.

sections.heading: Understand tarnish without over-polishing
sections.text: Silver can develop a darker surface when it reacts with sulfur-containing substances in its surroundings. Tarnish is a surface change; it is not, by itself, a reliable purity test. Removing tarnish repeatedly can also remove some underlying metal, so prevention and careful handling matter. A darker recess may be an intentional oxidised detail rather than dirt to remove.

sections.heading: Choose a gentle cleaning approach
sections.text: Begin with the care instructions and a soft cloth appropriate for the piece. A treatment intended for plain silver may be unsuitable for plating, an oxidised finish or a sensitive setting. Do not assume that a dip, abrasive paste or vigorous polishing is safe for every piece. If a cloth does not resolve the problem, describe the finish and setting to a jeweller before moving to a stronger treatment.

sections.heading: Store pieces clean, dry and separately
sections.text: Before putting jewellery away, make sure it is dry. Give each piece its own compartment or suitable soft pouch to reduce contact and tangling. Keep the storage space away from damp conditions and avoid contact with rubber bands. A neat routine also makes it easier to notice a bent clasp or a change in a setting before wearing the piece again.

sections.heading: When to ask for professional help
sections.text: Stop cleaning if a coating appears to be wearing away, a stone moves, or an unfamiliar surface change remains. Explain which cleaning products have already been used. Ask for advice specific to that piece rather than choosing a universal remedy. Keep the individual care instructions with the piece so that its next cleaning starts with the right information.

faqs.question: Does tarnish mean my silver jewellery is fake?
faqs.answer: Tarnish alone does not establish authenticity. Silver can tarnish naturally; use reliable product documentation and appropriate professional verification for authenticity questions.

faqs.question: Can I use the same cleaner on all silver jewellery?
faqs.answer: No. Plating, intentional oxidation and delicate settings can change which methods are suitable. Follow the instructions for the individual piece.

faqs.question: What is a useful everyday storage habit?
faqs.answer: Put pieces away dry and separated in suitable compartments or pouches, rather than leaving chains tangled together in a damp place.
